title: Diameter of Binary Tree
statement: The diameter is the length of the longest path between any two nodes, measured in edges. The path does not have to pass through the root. Return that length.
hints: The longest path through a node is the height of the left subtree plus the height of the right subtree, in edges.
The diameter of the tree is the maximum of that quantity over every node.
A height DFS can update a global best on the way back up. Height in edges from a node to its deepest leaf is what you return.

approaches.name: One DFS
approaches.explanation: Height and diameter are computed together.

editorial: Return the height of a subtree to the parent, and as a side effect record left_height + right_height. Use edges: a null child contributes height 0, and a leaf returns 1 to its parent if you count nodes, or you can count edges explicitly. The standard edge formulation returns 1 + max(left, right) as the height in edges from the parent link, and adds the two child heights.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def diameter_of_binary_tree(root: list) -> int:
    best = 0

    def height(node) -> int:
        nonlocal best
        if node is None:
            return 0
        left = height(node.left)
        right = height(node.right)
        best = max(best, left + right)
        return 1 + max(left, right)

    height(_build(root))
    return best
